question.text: In 'Vindhya Venture Fund', unit capital representing each LP's interest is required to be issued in:

answer.text: Physical certificate form only, signed by the trustee.
Either physical or demat, at the LP's option, under the Contribution Agreement.
Script-less form through the Investor Charter portal of SEBI.
Dematerialised mode only, with statements from the depository on a periodical basis.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the SEBI circular dated June 21, 2023, units representing unit capital held in the fund by an investor have to be issued in dematerialised mode only. Investors receive unit statements from the depository on a periodical basis. This compliance requirement — which protects investor interests — is specified as part of the subscription agreement. The Trap: Physical units are no longer permissible. There is no LP-option in the post-June 2023 regime. 'Investor Charter portal' is not a unit-issuance mechanism — Investor Charter is a separate disclosure document. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A both reference the June 2023 demat-of-units circular. XXI-B Portfolio Manager uses direct securities demat, not units, because PMS is not a pooled vehicle. Manager's Pro-Tip: Coordinate the demat corporate-action window between your DP and RTA especially around drawdown dates — late credit of units to LP demat accounts after money hits the fund bank can trigger beneficial-interest computation disputes.
